messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Severity: P0 — Elevated 5xx + TLS handshake failures from edge -> gateway in prod-us and prod-eu. See metrics: high TLS handshake errors and spikes in 525/524 from edge proxies. Auto-escalate to on-call.

pagerduty: Paging maya (oncall): high error rates affecting ~18% of requests to inference-gateway. Customer-facing latency/timeouts. Please ack and triage.

maya: acked. I'm on it — looking at the dashboard now. Can someone paste the top error logs?

jon: I grabbed the first 2 mins of logs. TL;DR: edge proxies showing 'tls: handshake failure' and gateway shows 'tls: unsupported certificate' for client auth in some pods. Also seeing connection resets.

maya: noting. Looks like spikes started ~06:52 UTC. Rolling deploy? cert rotation?

liam: no deploys. We had a scheduled CA rotation for internal mTLS last night but it was supposed to be staged and only for internal service mesh. Might be related.

sophia: Confirming — ops triggered a root CA rotation to rotate an intermediate yesterday evening. We tested on staging. Ops said they uploaded new CA bundle to SSM but I haven't seen the rotation checklist complete for prod.

eng-oncall: adding logs from the edge: ```
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-14T06:52:21Z ERROR tls_handshake: remote error: tls: bad certificate
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-14T06:52:22Z WARN connection_reset: upstream reset
[gateway] 2026-03-14T06:52:22Z ERROR mtls: client cert validation failed: unknown ca
```

maya: hmm, 'unknown ca' during client cert validation suggests the gateway or edge doesn't have the new CA chain. Could be a partial roll where edge got new CA but gateway workers still using old bundle, or vice versa.

jon: I'm seeing mixed success rates by availability zone. prod-us-west-1a shows elevated failures, us-west-1b less so. That smells like a staggered config rollout.

liam: I'll query the cert store. Which KMS key was used for the new CA? ops code referenced kms://rotations/ca-v2.

sophia: Confirmed: a subset of edge proxies pulled ca-v2 from SSM at 06:45, but the private gateway fleet pulls certs from the secrets service; the secrets service wasn't redeployed to pick up the new bundle. So mismatch plausible.

maya: OK plan: 1) short-term mitigation: fail requests with a graceful fallback to the legacy TLS profile that accepts both CA chains or disable client cert validation on the edge-to-gateway path for a small subset to drain traffic. 2) re-sync CA bundles to secrets service and restart gateway pods in a rolling fashion with canary traffic. 3) run post-force health checks and long-run cert rotation audit.

jon: For mitigation we can update the edge proxy TLS profile to include the old+new CA bundle (concatenate) without a code change. Patch rolling across 10% of edges first.

liam: I can push the concatenated CA bundle to SSM and trigger a config reload on edge-proxy. But we need owner sign-off for disabling strict client auth on gateway — that could temporarily allow unknown clients.

maya: Prioritize customer impact. We should apply the concat CA to edge first (low risk) so edge trusts both CA variants when initiating mTLS to gateway. That should reduce handshake failures. Then reconcile secrets service.

eng-oncall: Executing snippet to verify trust chain from an affected edge host: ```bash
# run on edge host
openssl s_client -connect gateway.prod.internal:443 -servername gateway.prod.internal -showcerts -CAfile /etc/edge/ca_bundle.pem
```

eng-oncall: Output shows: "verify return:1" when CAfile contains old CA only for some gateway pods, but "verify return:0 / depth=0: unable to get local issuer certificate" for others. Confirms inconsistent CA sets.

sophia: I'm pushing concatenated bundle to SSM at path /config/edge/ca-bundle/concat-v1 and issuing a rolling config reload. Pushing now.

liam: patch applied. Rolling reload started for edge-proxy group 'edge-primary-usw'. Rolling in 10% increments.

maya: I see latency dropping slightly and TLS handshake errors trending down in the first batch. Keep monitoring.

jon: Dashboard: 5xx rate from 18% -> 6% in 8 minutes in us-west. Other regions still elevated.

sophia: Secrets service now reconciled — I pushed the new CA bundle to secrets store and triggered a rolling restart of gateway pods with controlled concurrency (maxUnavailable=1). Doing canary in prod-eu first.

eng-oncall: Canary gateway pod in prod-eu back online, health checks green. No handshake failures reported on that pod.

liam: Starting restart of gateway pods in prod-us-west with 2s stagger.

maya: Heads-up: Customer impact assessment — currently degraded for about 22% of traffic at peak, primarily inference generation endpoints behind the gateway. Some customers reported timeouts. Our SLO alerting triggered.

jon: Drafting a short customer message for status page: "We are investigating TLS handshake failures impacting a subset of requests in prod regions. Mitigation work underway." Will post after we have more concrete ETA.

sophia: Gateway restarts progressing. After 3rd pod restart, TLS errors in prod-us-west down to <1%.

eng-oncall: Running smoke test: ```bash
curl -v --resolve gateway.prod.internal:443:10.0.5.12 https://gateway.prod.internal/health
# expect HTTP/200
```

eng-oncall: health OK on canary pods, and test inference request returns 200 and tokens.

maya: Great — start closing mitigation loop. What changed root cause-wise?

liam: Root cause: an incomplete rollout of CA rotation. Edge proxies began pulling concatenated bundles from SSM, but the secrets service that gateways use still had the old CA only. The mismatch caused client cert verification failures. Also our rotation orchestration didn't enforce atomicity across dependent services.

sophia: Contributing factors: missing preflight check in rotation runbook, and lack of a quick toggle to accept dual CA chains centrally.

maya: Postmortem action items (assignments inline):
- ops: add atomic rollout check + preflight verification for CA rotations (sophia)
- infra: add canary smoke test that validates mTLS handshake across gateway and edge before global rollout (jon)
- security: review rotation policy and add unit test for secrets-service propagation (liam)
- eng: implement a feature toggle to accept multiple CA roots for 1 deployment cycle (maya)
- runbook: document emergency mitigation steps (concat bundle and rolling restart) and add quick commands (jon)

jon: I'll post the status page update now with an ETA for full recovery (10-15m) and link to this thread.

sophia: status page updated. Message: "Mitigation deployed, traffic is returning to normal. We're continuing rolling restarts and will monitor for full recovery."

eng-oncall: Monitoring for 30m. We'll watch for regressions and CPU/memory churn after restarts.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged resolved (post-mitigation) — please run post-incident review.

maya: Thanks team. Taking the incident to postmortem. I will open a jira with the action items and owners. Marking incident P0 -> resolved. :white_check_mark:

liam: tagging follow-ups and adding links to rotation playbook.

sophia: leaving note: if anyone sees any late TLS drops, ping me directly.

maya: end of thread — timeline will be extracted for postmortem doc.
